reference_resolution.rule: decision_id must resolve to an actual ADR file under docs/decisions/; considered_options must each resolve to a real alternative discussed in that ADR — no orphan references (issue-515 invariant 2). Each axis_evaluation ref must resolve to a real entry inside this record carrying axis (must be in this role's judgment_axes), verdict (supports|contradicts|no-opinion), and citation (a docs/product/*.md entry path); when verdict is contradicts, the entry must also carry a finding object with target_path (must resolve against some role's write_scope) and a non-empty required_fix (issue-573 architecture proposal, sections 1 and 6).

recomputation.rule: outcome is recomputed from the referenced ADR's own status field, never asserted independently of the ADR text.
recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)

gate_b_contrast: hollow instance: considered_options listing exactly one option, or decision_drivers absent/boilerplate, is schema-conformant but not a real trade-off decision — MADR's own template (adr.github.io/madr) requires decision drivers and multiple considered options with pros/cons weighed against them, not merely named (issue-807 step2 audit).
gate_c_axis_evaluation: see docs/handbooks/architecture-methodology.md, section 'Axis evaluation procedure — maintenance_complexity' for the READ/EXECUTE/CRITERIA/CITATION method this role's axis_evaluation entries must follow, grounded in MADR's decision-drivers/considered-options weighing method rather than field names alone.

use_when.board_condition: a cross-module design choice is proposed on the branch AND no architecture record exists yet for that decision
